basic_info.name: Sunoh.ai
basic_info.description: Sunoh.ai is a doctor-side ambient AI medical scribe built by healow, the patient-engagement arm of ambulatory-EHR vendor eClinicalWorks (Westborough, Massachusetts), which listens to the live patient-provider conversation and drafts a structured progress note plus order capture (labs, imaging, procedures, medications, follow-up) that the physician reviews, edits and imports into the EHR. The single most load-bearing fact for MediKiosk Module C is its evidence posture: at very large adoption (vendor claims 100,000+ providers; eClinicalWorks press releases say 'over 90,000 providers') and a clear price point ($149/user/month), Sunoh publishes no accuracy benchmark, no model card and no peer-reviewed evaluation, while independent reviewers report note errors concentrated in the Assessment and Plan sections and an editing burden that can offset time saved - i.e. it is the deployed-but-unmeasured doctor-inside-the-encounter comparator against which a patient-side, elicitation-first, provenance-rich summary must be argued.
basic_info.organization: healow / eClinicalWorks (Sunoh.ai is presented as a subsidiary/brand of eClinicalWorks, Inc.; CEO and co-founder Girish Navani); headquarters Westborough, Massachusetts, USA
basic_info.country: United States (primary market); the same product is marketed in India through eClinicalWorks India, and LinkedIn lists a distributed workforce split across the US (~3 staff) and India (~2 staff)

technical_features.what_it_does: Sunoh.ai performs ambient listening during the patient encounter, transcribes the dialogue, distinguishes doctor from patient (filtering small talk), and drafts a clinical document in seconds: a visit transcript, a structured Progress Note categorised into sections, a draft SOAP note and a clinical summary, plus order capture for labs, imaging, procedures, medication orders and follow-up. The physician reviews, edits and approves the draft and then imports it into the EHR; the tool is EHR-agnostic and can also export a completed note as PDF. It is explicitly not a pre-visit, patient-elicited history tool and it does not generate an ABDM/FHIR summary document - it targets the encounter note inside an existing US EHR workflow.
technical_features.architecture: Cloud-based ambient AI using speech recognition plus NLP/LLM-style summarisation, hosted on Microsoft Azure, with mobile (iOS, Android), iPad and web-browser clients. Integration uses SMART on FHIR and OAuth 2.0 to launch from the patient chart and write discrete data back into EHR fields; native integrations exist for eClinicalWorks (deepest, native), athenahealth (via marketplace), Epic (FHIR), Cerner, ModMed, Practice Fusion and Tebra, and a free 'EHR Sync' Chrome extension pushes notes into any browser-based EHR. Vendor does not publish the ASR or note-generation models used, model sizes or architecture internals, so the model stack is a black box.
technical_features.inputs: Live doctor-patient conversation audio captured during the visit (via phone, iPad or desktop/browser), plus physician/patient context from the launching EHR and custom note templates; it is encounter audio, not patient-uploaded documents.
technical_features.outputs: Real-time transcript of the dialogue flow; draft clinical document/progress note organised into standard sections (including SOAP); draft clinical summary; order capture drafts (labs, imaging, procedures, medications, follow-up); exportable PDF; and discrete data written back into EHR fields (histories, allergies, medications, billing codes and order entries where integration depth allows, most natively on eClinicalWorks).
technical_features.standards_compliance: Interoperability is framed around SMART on FHIR and OAuth 2.0 for chart launch and data write-back, with native/epic FHIR connectivity. Security/compliance claims are limited to HIPAA (BAA signed; administrative, physical and technical safeguards claimed); SOC 2, GDPR and ISO 27001 are not publicly claimed, data residency is not specified, and the training-on-customer-data position is not publicly addressed. No ABDM, NRCeS FHIR R4 IG, OPConsultRecord, SNOMED CT, LOINC or ICD conformance is claimed for Sunoh.ai itself. eClinicalWorks India separately markets the broader eClinicalWorks HMIS as ABDM-certified and DPDP-ready with Azure India data centres, but no source confirms Sunoh.ai emits ABDM profile-validated or OPConsultRecord documents. [Sunoh.ai ABDM/NRCeS integration: uncertain - not documented]
technical_features.offline_capability: No offline capability. Sunoh is a cloud service on Microsoft Azure and independent reviewers note reliance on a stable internet connection; there is no documented local storage, on-premise, store-and-forward or offline mode. This is the clearest structural gap versus MediKiosk's offline-first constraint.
technical_features.languages_supported: Multilingual but global-US oriented: vendor and customer sources name Spanish, Mandarin, Portuguese and Cantonese as commonly used in FQHC settings, plus English, and claim recognition of different accents and dialects. Spanish support is the most frequently cited and most substantive (letting patients speak Spanish while the note is captured in English). No Hindi, Devanagari or Hinglish/code-mixed Indian-language capability is documented for Sunoh.ai itself, though the eClinicalWorks India HMIS marketing references multilingual Indian consultation capture at the platform level. [Indian-language / Hindi support for Sunoh.ai specifically: uncertain]
technical_features.deployment_model: Cloud SaaS; runs on Microsoft Azure. Clients: iOS and Android phones, iPad and web browser, plus a Chrome extension for EHR sync; marketed as working with any EHR (native on eClinicalWorks/athenahealth/Epic/Cerner/ModMed/Practice Fusion/Tebra, browser-extension fallback for other browser-based EHRs). It is a per-provider software subscription with no kiosk or fixed-hardware footprint; exact server hardware requirements are not published.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: No accuracy figure is published. Sunoh describes its documentation as 'highly accurate' but publishes no transcription accuracy percentage, no note-quality metric (ROUGE/BERTScore/clinical-fact recall), no model card, no named models and no evaluation methodology; independent reviewers (AI Health Index, Commure, Plaud) all flag this gap and one low-quality aggregator cites '>95%' unverified. The only concrete quality signal is negative: verified user reviews report documentation errors concentrated in Assessment and Plan sections, and at least one clinically meaningful error (a prescribed steroid ointment documented as a cream); one physician reported editing consumed nearly as much time as prior dictation. So the defensible summary is: adoption is large, but demonstrated accuracy evidence is absent. [Any Sunoh.ai accuracy figure: uncertain - none published]
performance_metrics.latency: Vendor-stated time-to-note is seconds after the encounter ('turns real conversations into accurate clinical notes in seconds'), with customer testimonials claiming notes can be completed within ~2 minutes of the visit ending, documentation 'up to 40% faster', and 90% of notes locked same-day (up from 72%) at one practice. eClinicalWorks reported a 33.2% improvement in documentation speed and providers handling 102.5% more appointments at its 2026 Health Center Summit. These are customer/vendor operational metrics on unspecified cloud hardware, not a published latency SLA. [Formal latency benchmark: uncertain]
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: Not published. Sunoh runs as a cloud (Azure) service, so there is no on-device model or minimum hardware spec disclosed; the client requirement in practice is a smartphone/tablet/browser with a microphone and internet, and reviewers note dependence on microphone quality and stable connectivity. No RAM, VRAM, CPU or model-size figure exists - a material unknown given MediKiosk's ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk budget.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Vendor homepage claims 100,000+ healthcare providers/providers using Sunoh.ai; eClinicalWorks press releases consistently state 'over 90,000 providers'. AI Health Index flags that Sunoh's own pages variously cite >50,000, >80,000 and >100,000 physicians with no date or denominator, so the headline adoption number is inconsistent and should be treated as approximate. Named deployments include mid-size FQHCs and practices (Family Health Centers 76/78-provider, Johnson Health Center 75/78-provider, Southeast Alabama Rural Health Associates, Boulder City Primary Care, plus testimonials from Oak Orchard, MedFlorida, St. Croix, Sun Life Health and others). Pricing page and homepage both cite '100,000+ providers'. Company size is small (LinkedIn lists ~8 employees, 11-50 range).
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: There is no evaluation protocol to grade: no peer-reviewed publication, no controlled comparison, no independent evaluation, no published accuracy benchmark, no fairness/subgroup analysis and no accuracy breakdown by language, accent or dialect was located across two review passes. Evidence is limited to vendor case studies and customer testimonials. AI Health Index graded Sunoh 'C' on the explicit precedent that scale of use and satisfaction anecdotes do not substitute for evidence of benefit, noting that category peers (Nabla, Microsoft Dragon Copilot) have randomised-trial evidence where Sunoh does not. For Module C this is the cautionary precedent: deployment scale without an evaluation harness is a defensible attack surface.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: Sunoh.ai is the scale benchmark and the negative example for Module C. It validates the commercial demand and the core signal-processing premise - that ambient AI can turn live clinical dialogue into structured, EHR-importable notes at 100k-provider scale and be sold profitably at $149/user/month - so the Module C team can assume the underlying ASR+summarisation task is real and monetisable. But it also demonstrates exactly the failure mode MediKiosk's constraints are designed to avoid: cloud-only (no offline), doctor-inside-the-encounter (no patient-elicited pre-consultation history), English/Western-language oriented (no Hindi/Hinglish evidence), and, most importantly, unmeasured quality (no accuracy benchmark, errors concentrated in Assessment and Plan). For Module C's 'elicit-never-diagnose + physician attestation + provenance' design, Sunoh is the proof that unnamed-model, unbenchmarked note generation is now widespread enough that a rigorous, published, offline, patient-side alternative can differentiate on trust and evidence rather than on the mere existence of a scribe.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (1) the workflow discipline of draft -> physician review/edit -> approve -> write-back, which is exactly Module C's physician-attestation lane and shows the review gate is the accepted clinical pattern; (2) SMART on FHIR + OAuth 2.0 as the launch/data-write integration pattern for any hospital/HIS-side screen; (3) the order-capture concept (turning spoken plan into pre-filled actionable orders) as a physician-facing convenience worth mirroring only in the physician-owned Assessment/Plan lane, gated by attestation. Adapt: Sunoh's operational metric set (time-to-note, notes locked same-day, documentation-time reduction) as evaluation dimensions, but replace its absent accuracy reporting with Module C's planned fidelity metrics (concept recall, omission checks, inference-aware hallucination). Reject: the black-box model with no published accuracy or model card; cloud-only execution that cannot satisfy offline-first; and any drift from 'elicit, never diagnose' - Sunoh auto-drafts Assessment and Plan content, which is precisely where its reported errors cluster, so Module C must keep Assessment and Plan physician-authored/draft-only rather than auto-generated.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Key weaknesses: (1) no published accuracy, model card or peer-reviewed evaluation, with user-reported errors concentrated in Assessment and Plan and at least one clinically meaningful medication-formulation error, plus editing burden that can offset time savings; (2) cloud-only, Azure-hosted, internet-dependent - no offline path; (3) data residency unspecified and no SOC 2/GDPR/ISO claims, only HIPAA, with training-on-customer-data unaddressed; (4) no ABDM/NRCeS/OPConsultRecord conformance and no documented Indian-language (Hindi/Devanagari) capability for Sunoh itself; (5) inconsistent adoption claims (>50k/>80k/>100k) undermine the headline number; (6) documentation/limits and warranty/indemnity commitments not published. These are exactly the claims Module C must be able to make (measured, offline, India-resident, profile-conformant) but cannot currently copy from any deployed peer.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: Sunoh.ai and MediKiosk barely overlap in workflow, so it mostly sharpens rather than erodes the differentiation. Sunoh is doctor-side and during-visit; MediKiosk is patient-side and pre-visit, so the total-time-to-summary and the elicitation burden are structurally different (MediKiosk moves history-taking off the 2-5 minute consult; Sunoh documents the consult itself). Sunoh is cloud-only, so MediKiosk's offline-first kiosk remains uncontested. Sunoh is US-EHR- and global-language-oriented with no ABDM/NRCeS emission, so MediKiosk's OPConsultRecord-plus-attester contract and India data residency are not matched. Sunoh publishes no accuracy metrics, so MediKiosk's intended per-field provenance, confidence and evaluation harness can be positioned as the trust differentiator. Net: Sunoh strengthens the case that structured AI documentation is table stakes and commercially proven, while its measured-evidence gap and cloud-only, encounter-bound design leave MediKiosk's stated differentiators intact.

business_info.license: Proprietary commercial software; closed source, no open-source or public license. No public API terms were located (API availability is not publicly disclosed).
business_info.pricing: $149 per user per month (marketed as a limited-time rate off a $199 list price) for the Standard Professional Plan; a Group and Enterprise Plan is custom-priced via direct sales with no public group rate. No free tier; a free no-commitment trial/demo is offered. Earlier third-party reporting cited a $149/user/month flat rate with a per-visit option, and one comparison site cites a per-visit price around $1.25 (unverified). Pricing page notes implementation services, 24x7 support, Azure hosting and a BAA are included.
business_info.funding: No separate external funding disclosed. Sunoh.ai is presented as a subsidiary/brand of eClinicalWorks (a privately held, long-established ambulatory EHR company), so it is effectively corporate-backed rather than venture-funded as a standalone startup. No rounds, amounts or valuations were located for Sunoh.ai itself. [Any Sunoh.ai-specific funding: uncertain - none disclosed]
business_info.commercial_status: Commercial paid product of a private EHR vendor (eClinicalWorks/healow), sold on a per-provider subscription on the open market to clinicians on any EHR and bundled/natively integrated for eClinicalWorks customers. Not free, not a government programme and not an unpaid project.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Direct ambient-scribe competitors: Abridge, Microsoft/Nuance DAX Copilot (Dragon Copilot), Ambience Healthcare, Nabla, DeepScribe, Commure Scribe, Augnito (India), and India's EkaScribe. Reviewers specifically contrast Sunoh (seven named EHR integrations, no published accuracy) with Commure Scribe (60+ EHRs, published benchmarks) and with Nabla / Microsoft Dragon Copilot (randomised-trial evidence). For MediKiosk, the more relevant overlap is with any product pushing a structured ABDM/FHIR summary (EkaScribe, ABDM-native entrants) rather than with the US ambient-scribe cohort, which competes on encounter documentation.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: Native EHR integrations with eClinicalWorks (deepest: notes, billing codes and orders map into discrete fields in one step), athenahealth (marketplace; writes histories, allergies and medications back), Epic (via open interoperability/FHIR), Cerner, ModMed, Practice Fusion and Tebra; plus a free 'EHR Sync' Chrome extension for any browser-based EHR. Hosted on Microsoft Azure; SMART on FHIR + OAuth 2.0 launch/write-back. India context: eClinicalWorks India markets the wider HMIS as ABDM-certified and DPDP-ready on Azure India data centres, but Sunoh.ai itself lists no ABDM/health-locker/consent-manager integration.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: Sunoh sits inside the US ambulatory-EHR ecosystem (eClinicalWorks/healow), whose distribution advantage is the main reason it reached 100k-provider scale - a distribution story, not a technical one. Two ecosystem signals matter for MediKiosk: (1) the ambient-scribe category is consolidating around large EHR/health-IT owners (Microsoft/Nuance, eClinicalWorks/healow) and is now a commodity feature, so MediKiosk should not compete on ambient encounter documentation; (2) the India wing of eClinicalWorks is actively marketing ABDM certification and DPDP readiness, meaning the ABDM/FHIR tailwind is now also reaching incumbent US vendors, which raises the bar for an SIH prototype to demonstrate hard profile conformance rather than generic 'ABDM-ready' claims. Sunoh's unmeasured accuracy also creates an opening: the Indian market has no equivalent public accuracy benchmark for encounter-to-note quality, so a published, reproducible evaluation is a differentiator.

history.release_date: Sunoh.ai was founded/launched around 2023 (comparison sites list 'Founded 2023'); the vendor site has been publicly available since at least late 2023-2024 (homepage assets dated 2023-12). [Exact first public release date: uncertain]
history.key_milestones: ~2023 - Sunoh.ai founded as healow/eClinicalWorks' ambient-scribe product. 2024-2025 - expansion from eClinicalWorks-native to EHR-agnostic (athenahealth, Epic, Cerner, ModMed, Practice Fusion, Tebra + EHR Sync extension); adoption claims grow from 50k to 100k+ providers; mobile iOS/Android apps. 2026-01-14 - Boulder City Primary Care case (27% efficiency, 90% same-day notes). 2026-02-04 - Southeast Alabama Rural Health Associates case (15% efficiency). 2026-03-18 - Johnson Health Center 75/78-provider FQHC case (5-10 min/patient saved). 2026-04-24 - deep-EHR-integration blog articulating SMART on FHIR/OAuth architecture. 2026-04-27 - eClinicalWorks India push positioning Sunoh.ai for Indian multilingual clinics. 2026-05-07 - Family Health Centers 76-provider FQHC case (>95% of visits). 2026-05-21 - eClinicalWorks Health Center Summit data: 102.5% more appointments handled, 33.2% documentation speed improvement. 2026 pricing standardised at $149/user/month (from $199).
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: Within the last six months (since ~2026-03-16): (1) 2026-03-18 - Johnson Health Center FQHC case study (5-10 min saved per patient visit; claimed faster and more accurate than prior solutions especially for HPI). (2) 2026-04-24 - a vendor blog formalising the 'deep EHR integration' pitch around SMART on FHIR + OAuth 2.0 and discrete-data mapping. (3) 2026-04-27 - an eClinicalWorks India article marketing Sunoh.ai for Indian multilingual clinics integrated with eClinicalWorks India HMIS. (4) 2026-05-07 - Family Health Centers case (>95% of visits, Spanish-language support). (5) 2026-05-21 - eClinicalWorks Health Center Summit presented operational data: providers using Sunoh handled 102.5% more appointments and achieved a 33.2% documentation-speed improvement. (6) 2026-05 onward - eClinicalWorks India messaging around ABDM-certified, DPDP-ready paperless-hospital deployments on Azure India data centres. What did NOT change: no accuracy benchmark, no model card, no peer-reviewed evaluation, and no offline or ABDM-native capability was published in this window.

market_positioning.target_users: Individual physicians, primary-care and specialty practices, and larger groups/hospitals - especially Federally Qualified Health Centers and multi-provider clinics in the US; secondarily eClinicalWorks India clinics. It is a clinician/health-system tool, not a patient-facing product.
market_positioning.market_segment: Ambient clinical scribing / AI clinical documentation (encounter note generation and order capture), sitting inside the broader AI-powered EHR and medical-transcription segment. It does not play in patient intake, PHR, document digitisation, AYUSH software, diagnostics kiosks or FHIR-summary tooling.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: Sunoh pitches itself as '#1 Trusted by 100k+ Doctors', 'the AI medical scribe', 'saving doctors 2+ hours daily', promising to 'free you from the keyboard so you can focus on your patients - not your screen', to 'reduce burnout', 'reclaim your time', and to 'finish your notes at the office'. It emphasises seamless/native EHR integration ('deep, native-feeling, bidirectional EHR integration that puts discrete data right where it belongs'), mobile-first capture, multilingual support and HIPAA/BAA assurance. The eClinicalWorks India variant is pitched as an 'invisible assistant' that handles multilingual Indian consultations and pushes drafts directly into the eClinicalWorks India HMIS.
